summary: @servicetitan/react-hooks preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime binary from a GitHub release (oven-sh/bun v1.3.13) into a temporary directory, marks it executable, and then invokes `execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'])` to run a sibling file under Bun. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line, heavily obfuscated blob using string-array rotation (`n7gIxM` array with `WV8StW` rotator) and `_0xNNNN`-style identifiers, with no readable strings, no imports, and none of the react-hooks code implied by the package name. The obfuscated payload is invoked only by the preinstall path via the freshly-downloaded Bun binary, never through the package's declared exports. Executing an obfuscated blob under a smuggled alternate runtime at install time bypasses Node-based scanners and delivers arbitrary attacker-controlled code to the installer's machine on `npm install`. The package is published in the @servicetitan scope and advertises itself as a react-hooks library, but the shipped install-time behavior is unrelated to that purpose, consistent with a compromised-maintainer or scope-hijack attack.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
